# Start-SqlServiceMonitor

<!-- Generated by tools/Build-Catalog.ps1. Edit the script header, not this file. -->

Ensures all SQL Server services are running. Retries for 30 seconds and logs an error for any that fail to start.

| | |
|---|---|
| Location | `scripts/windows/server/Start-SqlServiceMonitor.ps1` |
| Platform | Windows (SQL Server host) |
| Permissions | Local administrator (writes to the Application event log, source SQLServiceMonitor) |
| Safety | Changes data (starts stopped services; supports -WhatIf) |

## When to use

After patching or reboots, to bring SQL services back up and log an error for any that won't start.

## Description

Discovers all SQL Server-related services, attempts to start any that are stopped,
polls every 5 seconds for up to 30 seconds, and writes an Error entry to the Event Log
(and the log file) for any service that fails to reach a Running state in time.

Exit code 0 means every SQL service is running; 1 means at least one failed to start.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-TimeoutSeconds` | Int32 | No | How long (in seconds) to wait for each service to reach Running state. Default: 30. |
| `-PollIntervalSeconds` | Int32 | No | How often (in seconds) to check service status during the wait. Default: 5. |
| `-ExcludedService` | String[] | No | Service names that must NOT be started automatically (for example a deliberately stopped instance). |
| `-OutputPath` | String | No | Folder for the daily log file. Falls back to $env:TOOLBOX_REPORT_DIR, then prompts. |
| `-CustomerName` | String | No | Optional. Adds a &lt;OutputPath&gt;\&lt;CustomerName&gt; subfolder. |

## Examples

```powershell
.\Start-SqlServiceMonitor.ps1 -OutputPath D:\Logs
```

```powershell
.\Start-SqlServiceMonitor.ps1 -TimeoutSeconds 60 -PollIntervalSeconds 10 -OutputPath D:\Logs -ExcludedService 'SQLBROWSER' -WhatIf
```
